headline: P0035 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 19.7% against 6.0% expected for its patient mix, with the excess mostly in mid-complexity patients rather than low-complexity ones; inconclusive without documentation
rationale: P0035 billed 12 of 61 claims (19.7%) as 99215. The expected share for its patient complexity is 6.0% (z vs peers 2.17, risk-adjusted score 1.69). Within each complexity group from 1 to 5+ chronic conditions, the provider's 99215 share is above the all-provider share. The largest gap is at 3 conditions: 5 of 16 visits (31.2%) against 8.7% for all providers. This is a pattern consistent with some upward coding that the patient mix does not explain. However, the low-complexity signal that would most suggest upcoding is weak. There were no 99215s on 0-condition patients and only 1 of 11 visits on 1-condition patients. That one claim, C0017162, is a 42-year-old with type 2 diabetes plus a UTI code (N39.0). The same patient had a 99214 the day before (C0017147), which is worth checking. The sampled 99215s on high-complexity patients (C0017114, C0017161, C0017119, C0017160) involve patients with 4 to 6 chronic conditions, including heart failure and atrial fibrillation. These look plausible, although C0017119 lists only E11.9. Some sampled lower-level claims also raise questions. C0017165 is a 99214 for a 0-condition patient with only a URI code (J06.9). Meanwhile, C0017131 and C0017168 billed 99213 for patients with 4 or more conditions. Counts per group are small, the claim lists are samples rather than every claim, and the packet has no clinical notes, time or MDM documentation, so it cannot show whether the levels were supported.
next_steps: Request and review medical records for all 12 billed 99215 claims, especially the 5 at 3 chronic conditions and C0017162, to check whether MDM or total time supports level 5.
Check C0017162 against C0017147 (same patient, consecutive days, 99215 after a 99214) for duplicate or split services and medical necessity.
Review whether diagnosis coding on high-level claims shows the complexity billed (e.g., C0017119 lists only E11.9 despite 4 chronic conditions).
Look at the 99214 share (33 of 61 claims) against peers, and sample 99214s on low-complexity patients such as C0017165 (0 conditions, URI only).
Pull the full claim history, not just the sample, to confirm the distribution by complexity group and any trend over time before escalating.
